content.title: Soldier Boy’s Fate & How It Sets Up The Boys Season 5’s MacGuffin Explained By Eric Kripke
content.text: Credit: Jasper Savage/Prime Video Published Apr 8, 2026, 11:54 PM EDT Matthew Rudoy is one of ScreenRant's Movie & TV News Editors. He covers the latest in movie & TV news, with a focus on major franchises like Star Wars, The Boys, and Game of Thrones. He wrote lists for ScreenRant from 2017-2022, became a news writer in 2023, a senior staff writer in 2024, and an editor in 2025. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Warning: There are spoilers ahead for The Boys season 5, episode 2, "Teenage Kix."Soldier Boy (Jensen Ackles) is back, and showrunner Eric Kripke explains how his fate sets up the rest of The Boys season 5. Homelander (Antony Starr) takes Soldier Boy out of his cryogenically frozen state to track down Billy Butcher (Karl Urban), but things take a deadly turn when Ackles' character is exposed to a virus that can kill supes. He initially appears to have been killed by the virus, but the end of The Boys season 5, episode 2, proves otherwise, as he sits up while encased inside a body bag. In an interview with TV Insider, Kripke was asked about the implications of Soldier Boy surviving the lethal virus. The showrunner confirms that the character isn't dead and the reason he is immune to the virus sets up "the primary MacGuffin of the season" that Homelander and the Boys will race to find. Check out Kripke's comments below: The Boys season 5 trailers teased that Homelander would be searching for V1, Vought's first iteration of Compound V, and that it could make him immortal. This is likely the primary MacGuffin and the source of Soldier Boy's immunity that Kripke is hinting at. Since Soldier Boy is one of Vought's original supes, it makes sense that he was injected with V1, and it is why he survived the virus when the Teenage Kix supes in the room did not. Homelander will seemingly be impossible to defeat if he finds V1 and injects himself with it, thereby making him immune to the virus. Beyond stopping Homelander, Kripke brings up the possibility of the MacGuffin being able to protect Annie January/Starlight (Erin Moriarty), Kimiko (Karen Fukuhara), and Butcher from the virus despite the Compound V in their blood. Butcher has a terminal brain tumor and limited time left to live, but Annie and Kimiko may still have long futures if they survive the fight ahead and get immunity through V1. It’s never over. There’s always someone who needs to be reminded who’s in charge REVEAL MY CHARACTER → Vought Psychological Profile Complete Your Boys Alter Ego ⚡ Homelander “I can do whatever I want.” You crave control and validation in equal measure. On the surface, you project confidence and power — the kind that makes people either worship you or cower. But underneath? There’s a void that no amount of adoration can fill. You demand loyalty but struggle to give it. You’re at your most dangerous when you feel cornered, and at your most human when you realize that all the power in the world can’t make someone genuinely love you. You’re not the hero — you’re the cautionary tale.Narcissistic Terrifying Charismatic Unstable 🔨 Billy Butcher “I’m gonna f***in’ kill you all.” You’re a wrecking ball with a grudge, and God help anyone standing between you and your target. Your rage is legendary — but so is the pain that fuels it. You’d burn the world down for the people you love, and that’s both your greatest strength and your fatal flaw. You don’t play by the rules because the rules were written by the people you’re fighting against. Underneath all that bravado is someone who’s terrified of losing anyone else.Ruthless Driven Self-Destructive Loyal ✨ Starlight “I’m done being controlled.” You walked into a corrupt system believing you could change it from the inside — and against all odds, you might be right. You’ve been lied to, manipulated, and betrayed, but none of it broke your moral compass. You fight not because you enjoy it, but because someone has to stand up. You’re the kind of person who sees the worst in people and still chooses to believe in the best. That’s not naivety — that’s courage.Brave Principled Resilient Compassionate 🎵 Hughie Campbell “I don’t want to be a person who can just let things go.” You never asked for any of this. You were living a quiet life, and then the world showed you something so unjust that you couldn’t look away. You’re not the strongest or the loudest, but you have something most people lack: the stubborn refusal to accept that this is just how things are. You’re terrified most of the time, but you show up anyway. That’s not weakness — that’s the definition of bravery. You fumble, you doubt, but you never quit.Anxious Resourceful Moral Brave 🌸 Kimiko “You are my heart.” You’ve been through horrors that would destroy most people, and yet here you are — still fighting, still caring, still protecting the ones you love. You don’t need words to communicate what matters; your actions say everything. You’re a contradiction in the most beautiful way: capable of devastating violence, but driven by an overwhelming tenderness. The world tried to make you a weapon, but you chose to be a person. That choice is the bravest thing anyone can do.LethalGentleProtectiveTraumatized ↻ PLAY AGAIN While The Boys season 5 is focused on wrapping up the story it's been telling since 2019, ​​​​​​​it is also setting up the story of Vought Rising, the upcoming prequel series featuring Soldier Boy in the 1950s and in the earlier days of Vought. The spinoff, which Kripke previously shared will debut in 2027, can reveal more about V1, why it was abandoned in favor of other iterations of Compound V, and any ways it affected Soldier Boy at this earlier stage in his life. Other members of The Boys' cast of characters who are expected to be involved in the search for V1 include Hughie Campbell (Jack Quaid), Mother's Milk (Laz Alonso), and Frenchie (Tomer Capone). Sister Sage (Susan Heyward) will probably be very interested in it as well, as it has the potential to be a major variable in her long-term schemes and pursuit of power. The Boys releases new episodes Wednesdays on Prime Video.
